list.description: Read reports and find the report IDs you need.
list.details: Team mode needs reports:read. The result is JSON.

report.description: Send a progress report from a JSON file.
report.details:
Team mode needs reports:write. Use one source_id for one report.
Reuse it to correct or retry that report. Pick a new one for new progress.

Example report.json:
  {"source_id":"website-review-20261128","title":"Reviewed the homepage","body":"Checked the links and shared the results."}

Run coflow list to read back the saved report.

comment.usage: coflow comment --id REPORT_ID --body "Thanks for the update"
comment.details:
Team mode needs comments:write. Run coflow list to find the report ID.
After a timeout, check whether your comment was saved before sending it again.

whoami.description: Check which user and space your credential belongs to.
whoami.details: Team mode needs one module read permission. This shows the current role and server features. Check the user and space before making changes.

workspace show.description: Find the project, domain and member values you can use.
workspace show.details: Team mode needs one module read permission. Copy a project ID from this result for --project.

todo board.description: Find column IDs and the latest board revision.

todo list.details: Use next_cursor from the result with --cursor to read the next page.

todo show.description: Read a task, its current revision and related records.

todo create.description: Create a task using a stable work ID.
todo create.recovery: Run coflow todo list to find the existing task before trying again.
todo create.details: Run coflow todo board first to find the column. Example file: {"title":"Review homepage","column_id":"COLUMN_ID","source_id":"homepage-review","operation_id":"homepage-create-1"}

todo change.description: Edit, move, submit or reopen a task using its current revision.
todo change.recovery: Run coflow todo show --id ID and coflow todo board before trying another change.
todo change.details: Put expected_revision from the latest record and a unique operation_id in the JSON file. Keep the same ID and file if the result of a request is unknown. Example file for a move: {"action":"move","column_id":"COLUMN_ID","board_revision":1,"expected_revision":1,"operation_id":"homepage-move-1"}. Use current revisions. The comment action needs comments:write and todos:read in place of todos:write. For scheduling use action edit and a schedule object.

report list.description: Read recent reports and find their IDs.

report show.description: Read a report and its links.

report upsert.description: Send or correct a progress report.
report upsert.recovery: Run coflow report list to check whether your report was saved before trying again.
report upsert.details: Use one source_id for one report. Read back the report with coflow report show --id ID. Use todo_ids in the file to link it to existing tasks. Example file: {"source_id":"homepage-check","title":"Checked the homepage","body":"All links were checked.","todo_ids":["TODO_ID"]}

report comment.recovery: Run coflow report show --id ID to check whether the comment was saved.
report comment.details: Copy the report ID from coflow report list.

calendar list.description: Read planned work and calendar nodes.
calendar list.details: The start date is included. The end date is excluded. Use YYYY-MM-DD. The default time zone is UTC. Team mode needs todos:read or calendar:read for the corresponding records. Send the same query, next_cursor and revision for the next page.

calendar show.description: Read the details of a calendar node.

calendar create.recovery: Run coflow calendar list for the date range and check whether the node was saved.

calendar change.description: Edit or archive a calendar node.
calendar change.recovery: Run coflow calendar show --id ID to read the latest node.
calendar change.details: Put expected_revision from the latest record and a unique operation_id in the JSON file. Keep the same ID and file if the result of a request is unknown.

context search.description: Find knowledge by project or keyword.
context search.details: Use --state active to find confirmed entries. Use next_offset for the next page while it is less than total.

context show.description: Read a knowledge entry and the records behind it.

context create.recovery: Run coflow context search to check whether the entry was saved.
context create.details: Example file: {"title":"Homepage review rule","body":"Verify links before delivery.","kind":"rule","state":"pending","visibility":"team","source_id":"homepage-rule","operation_id":"homepage-rule-create-1"}

context change.description: Update knowledge using the latest record.
context change.recovery: Run coflow context show --id ID and keep any newer edits.
context change.details: Put expected_revision from the latest record and a unique operation_id in the JSON file. Keep the same ID and file if the result of a request is unknown. Use the existing entry as the basis for an edit. An Agent token can save entries for human review.

data summary.details: The start date is included. The end date is excluded. Use YYYY-MM-DD. The default time zone is UTC. The server counts modules your credential can read. Current snapshots and events in the period are separate.

data detail.description: Read the original links behind one count.
data detail.details: The start date is included. The end date is excluded. Use YYYY-MM-DD. The default time zone is UTC. Send next_offset and revision together on the next page with the same filters.

handoff read.description: Read the facts needed to pick up existing work.
handoff read.details: Choose one task or project. Check the returned limits, then open the original records. A task lookup needs todos:read.

handoff changes.description: Check for updates after your last read.
handoff changes.details: Start without a cursor to make a baseline. Re-read changed records. After processing a page, use --checkpoint NAME --save-cursor NEXT_CURSOR with the same filters. The next read with --checkpoint NAME starts at that cursor.

todo column-create.details: Read the current board revision first. Use --file - to read the JSON object from stdin. Example JSON: {"name":"Verify","board_revision":1,"operation_id":"column-create-1"}

todo column-change.description: Edit, move or archive a board column.
todo column-change.details: Read current board and column revisions first. Go checks ownership and role. Use --file - to read the JSON object from stdin.

report edit.description: Edit a report by its record ID.
report edit.details: Read the current report and preserve its latest expected_updated_at. Use --file - to read the JSON object from stdin. Print a review request with --prepare. Open Agent credentials in CoFlow, paste the request and confirm it with your browser login.

report status.details: Use --file - to read the JSON object from stdin. Example JSON: {"status":"review"}

calendar reschedule.description: Change the planned dates for several tasks together.
calendar reschedule.details: Read the current revisions first. Go applies up to 25 rows together. Any conflict leaves all rows unchanged. Use null to clear a schedule. Use --file - to read the JSON object from stdin. Example JSON: {"operation_id":"reschedule-1","changes":[{"id":"TODO_ID","expected_revision":1,"schedule":null}]} Print a review request with --prepare. Open Agent credentials in CoFlow, paste the request and confirm it with your browser login.

calendar reports.details: Use YYYY-MM-DD, with an exclusive end date. Reuse the filters when following next_cursor.

auth login.description: Sign in to CoFlow from a browser, even when the CLI runs on another machine.
auth login.details: Use COFLOW_URL for your CoFlow address. Run this from a private terminal. Open the printed page, enter the short code and check the account and space before you allow access. Default access is read-only for seven days. For explicit write access, try --scope "reports:read reports:write". Access can last 1 to 30 days.

space list.description: List spaces with a saved CLI login on this server.
space list.details: Run coflow auth login --space TEAM_ID to add a space, then coflow space use --space TEAM_ID to select it.

space use.description: Select which saved space the CLI should use by default.
space use.details: Checks the login and saves only the selected space ID. Add --space TEAM_ID to any business command to override it.

auth grant.usage: coflow auth grant --space TEAM_ID --todo TODO_ID [--days 1] [--scope SCOPES]
auth grant.description: Ask a person to allow this CLI to work on one task or one project's tasks.
auth grant.details: Choose --todo TODO_ID or --project PROJECT_ID. Default is read-only for one day. Ask for --scope "todos:read todos:write" to edit allowed task fields. Keep this login under the Agent's own OS account.

auth logout.description: Revoke this CLI login and remove its local credential.
auth logout.details: This affects the saved browser login for COFLOW_URL. You can also revoke it from Agent credentials in CoFlow.

auth status.description: Check the saved CLI login online and see when it expires.
auth status.details: Use coflow whoami to check your effective identity, including when an Agent Token is supplied.

workspace bind.description: Remember this server and space for commands run from this directory.
workspace bind.details: First sign in to the target space. The local binding saves server, team and user IDs. Run coflow whoami here to verify it.

workspace unbind.description: Clear the server and space selected for this directory.
workspace unbind.details: Saved CLI logins stay available in coflow space list.

update check.description: Find out if a newer stable CoFlow release is available.
update check.details: Checks the official GitHub release. Server compatibility is unknown until you read the release notes.
